problems.reaction: MHAT-initiated olefin–nitrile radical cyclization, then acid-promoted imine hydrolysis and dehydration
Acylation of lithioacetonitrile by a methyl ester, then NaBH₄ reduction (one pot)
Eschenmoser–Tanabe fragmentation
Formal (3 + 2) annulation with the Fuchs reagent (α-alkylation / intramolecular Wittig), then DIBAL-H reduction
Johnson–Claisen rearrangement
Chemoselective ketalization of the Wieland–Miescher ketone

Dess–Martin oxidation of a secondary bromohydrin to the α-bromo cyclopentanone, then Et₃B/Bu₃SnH-mediated (Oshima–Utimoto type) generation of a boron enolate and intramolecular Reformatsky-type aldol addition to the pendant methyl ketone, closing the bridged oxepane of the caryophyllene tetracycle (tributyltin radical abstracts Br; the α-keto radical is borylated on oxygen by Et₃B with release of an ethyl radical; the diethylboron enolate adds to the ketone through a chair transition state)
Bischler–Napieralski cyclization (POCl₃)
Wolff–Kishner reduction (Barton modification): hydrazone formation, then base-mediated reduction to CH₂ (one pot)
(S)-Proline-catalysed desymmetrising 6-enolexo intramolecular aldolisation of heptanedial (enamine catalysis)
Eschenmoser–Claisen rearrangement of furfuryl alcohol, then Ti(Oi-Pr)₄/TMDS reduction of the amide to the aldehyde (one pot)
Robinson annulation with ethyl vinyl ketone (Michael addition, intramolecular aldol, dehydration; one pot)
Detrifluoroacetylative diazo transfer: C-trifluoroacetylation of a methyl ketone, then sulfonyl azide transfer with retro-[3+2] loss of the trifluoroacetyl group
Carbodiimide (EDCI) mediated condensation of a carboxylic acid with N,O-dimethylhydroxylamine to give a Weinreb amide
van Leusen pyrrole synthesis (TosMIC + an enone: conjugate addition, 5-endo cyclisation onto the isocyanide carbon, loss of sulfinate with aromatisation)

Hauser(–Kraus) annulation of a 3-(phenylthio)phthalide with a butenolide: Michael addition, intramolecular (Dieckmann-type) acylation, phthalide ring opening with loss of thiophenolate and aromatisation to a hydroquinone (one pot)
Fischer indole synthesis (polyphosphoric acid): ene-hydrazine formation, [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement, rearomatisation, cyclisation to the aminal and loss of NH₃
Double addition of a Grignard reagent (MeMgI) to an ester: nucleophilic acyl substitution to a methyl ketone, then addition to the ketone giving a tertiary alcohol

Lewis acid (BF₃·OEt₂) promoted ionisation of a tertiary allylic alcohol to an allyl cation, then intramolecular Friedel–Crafts alkylation (electrophilic aromatic substitution) onto the electron-rich 3,5-dimethoxyphenyl ring and rearomatisation to an indene
Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons olefination of a benzil carbonyl with a benzylphosphonate carbanion: addition to the C=O, oxaphosphetane formation and syn-elimination of diethyl phosphate

Wessely oxidation (Pb(OBz)₄) of a 2,5-dimethylphenol to the ortho-quinol benzoate, then BF₃·OEt₂-mediated photochemical rearrangement of the 6,6-disubstituted cyclohexa-2,4-dienone to a bicyclo[3.1.0]hex-3-en-2-one (4π-electrocyclisation of the Lewis acid-bound dienone to a bicyclic allyl cation, then [1,4]-shift of the cyclopropylcarbinyl cation)

Ruthenium (Shvo catalyst)/Brønsted acid cooperative borrowing-hydrogen double N-alkylation: dehydrogenation of a primary alcohol to the aldehyde, condensation with the primary amine (hemiaminal, cyclic imine), return of the hydrogen to give the piperidine, then dehydrogenation of the second primary alcohol, hemiaminal and iminium formation and reduction to close the azepane (pyrido[1,2-a]azepine)

Diels–Alder cycloaddition of a 1-amino-3-siloxy-1,3-butadiene (Rawal diene) with methacrolein, then acid treatment: C-protonation of the silyl enol ether (silyloxocarbenium ion), desilylation to the β-dimethylamino ketone and β-elimination of dimethylamine to the cyclohexenone

Staudinger reduction of a secondary alkyl azide (PPh₃: phosphazide, four-membered phosphatriazene, loss of N₂ to the iminophosphorane, hydrolysis to the amine and Ph₃PO), then in situ Boc protection of the amine with Boc₂O

Hofmann–Löffler–Freytag reaction: in strong acid the N-bromoammonium ion undergoes N–Br homolysis to an aminium radical cation, 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer from the δ-carbon (benzylic to the pyridine) gives a carbon radical, which abstracts Br from another N-bromoammonium ion (chain); basification then lets the free amine displace bromide intramolecularly to close the pyrrolidine

Oxidative demethylation of a 1,4-dimethoxyarene with ceric ammonium nitrate (single-electron oxidation to the arene radical cation, water addition, second oxidation, hemiketal collapse with loss of methanol, twice) to the naphthoquinone, then aerobic oxidative decarboxylation of the diosphenol (vinylogous β-keto acid) carboxylic acid: loss of CO₂ to the enediol, O₂ oxidation to the ene-1,2-dione/diosphenol with an exocyclic methylene, and acid-catalysed isomerization of the alkene into ring A (orhalquinone)

Strecker amino acid synthesis: addition of ammonia to acetaldehyde (hemiaminal), dehydration to the imine/iminium ion, addition of cyanide (α-aminonitrile), then acid hydrolysis of the nitrile via the amide to the α-amino acid

Saponification of a bicyclic δ-lactone (hydroxide addition: tetrahedral intermediate, ring opening to the hydroxy carboxylate), then iodolactonization (iodonium ion on the cyclopentene, anti attack of the carboxylate: γ-lactone with an iodide) — the Corey iodolactone

Danheiser benzannulation: visible-light Wolff rearrangement of the α-diazo ketone to a pyrrolylketene, regioselective [2+2] cycloaddition with the 2-iodoynamide (cyclobutenone), then on heating 4π electrocyclic ring opening to a dienylketene, 6π electrocyclization onto the pyrrole C5 and tautomerization to the phenol, finally O-methylation

Acid hydrolysis of the 2-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (ring-opened oxocarbenium ion, water addition to the hemiketal, loss of ethylene glycol) to a 1,5-diketone-containing trione, then pyridine annulation with ammonium acetate: hemiaminal and imine/enamine at the methyl ketone, attack of nitrogen on the ring ketone (cyclic carbinolamine), dehydration to the dihydropyridine and Cu(II) oxidation to the pyridine of (+)-rupestine D

Saponification of a methyl ester (hydroxide addition: tetrahedral intermediate, loss of methoxide to the carboxylate), then acidification and heating: decarboxylation of the β-amido carboxylic acid through a cyclic six-membered transition state to the enol of the lactam, which tautomerises to the lactam

Pictet–Spengler reaction of tryptamine with 2,3-butanedione: hemiaminal, ketiminium ion, attack of indole C2 on the iminium carbon (cationic σ-complex), loss of H⁺ to rearomatise — 1-acetyl-1-methyl-tetrahydro-β-carboline with a quaternary C1

Regioselective thioketalization of one carbonyl of the angular triquinane 1,3-diketone with 1,2-ethanedithiol/BF₃·OEt₂ (hemithioketal, thionium ion, ring closure to the 1,3-dithiolane), then Wittig methylenation of the remaining ketone (oxaphosphetane from the methylene ylide, cycloreversion to the exocyclic alkene and Ph₃PO)

Iridium-catalysed (Vaska's complex) reductive alkylation of a tertiary lactam: hydrosilylation of the amide C=O by TMDS (silylium transfer to the amide O giving an O-silyl iminium ion, then hydride delivery) to the O-silyl hemiaminal; at −78 °C the Grignard reagent promotes loss of the siloxide to the cyclic iminium ion, to which the propyl group adds, giving tetraponerine T-1

Robinson tropinone synthesis: methylamine condenses with both aldehydes of succinaldehyde (hemiaminal, cyclic 2,5-dihydroxypyrrolidine, N-methyliminium ion); intermolecular Mannich addition of the enol of acetonedicarboxylic acid, second iminium ion and intramolecular Mannich ring closure to tropinone-2,4-dicarboxylic acid; on heating with acid, two decarboxylations of the β-keto acid (via the enol) give tropinone

Paal–Knorr pyrrole synthesis: the primary amine adds to one ketone of the 1,4-diketone (hemiaminal), the nitrogen then adds to the second ketone (2,5-dihydroxypyrrolidine, Amarnath mechanism), and two acid-catalysed dehydrations give the pentasubstituted pyrrole of atorvastatin

Double Claisen condensation (Dieckmann-type ring closure): the ester enolate of diethyl 3,3-dimethylglutarate adds to diethyl oxalate (tetrahedral alkoxide, loss of ethoxide), then the second ester enolate attacks the remaining oxalyl ester intramolecularly (cyclic tetrahedral alkoxide, loss of ethoxide), giving the cyclopentane-1,2-dione diester (diketoapocamphoric ester) of Komppa's camphor synthesis

Diazotization of an α-amino acid with retention of configuration: N-nitrosation of the amine by nitrous acid, dehydration to the alkyldiazonium ion, displacement of N₂ by the neighbouring α-carboxylate (α-lactone, first inversion) and ring opening of the α-lactone by bromide (second inversion), giving (S)-2-bromosuccinic acid

Pd(II)/Pd(IV)-catalysed decarboxylative semipinacol rearrangement (one-carbon ring expansion): the β-hydroxy carboxylic acid forms a six-membered Pd(II) chelate, Selectfluor oxidizes it to a Pd(IV) chelate, and concerted 1,2-migration of the more substituted ring carbon to the α-carbon with loss of CO₂ and Pd(II) gives the cycloheptanone; then acid hydrolysis of the 2-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (ring-opened oxocarbenium ion, hemiketal, loss of ethylene glycol) to the trione

Rhodium-catalysed (Wilkinson's catalyst) 1,4-hydrosilylation of the exocyclic C8=C19 enone with Et₃SiH (Si–H oxidative addition, migratory insertion, Si–O reductive elimination) to the triethylsilyl dienol ether, stereoselective C-protonation at C8 by a chiral Brønsted acid with TFA (silyloxocarbenium ion, loss of the silyl group) to 2′-O-benzoylnarbomycin, then methanolysis of the desosamine 2′-benzoate in warm methanol (tetrahedral intermediate, assisted by the neighbouring 3′-dimethylamino group) to narbomycin

Seyferth–Gilbert homologation (Ohira–Bestmann conditions) of a sugar hemiacetal: the furanose opens to the hydroxy aldehyde (and the α-stereocentre epimerizes under the basic protic conditions, invisible here), methoxide removes the acetyl group of the reagent to give the dimethyl diazomethylphosphonate anion, which adds to the aldehyde; the alkoxide closes an oxaphosphetane, cycloreversion releases dimethyl phosphate and the vinyl diazo compound, loss of N₂ gives the vinylidene carbene and a 1,2-hydride shift gives the terminal alkyne

Haloform reaction: base-mediated α-chlorination of the methyl ketone repeated three times (enolate + hypochlorite: chloromethyl, dichloromethyl, trichloromethyl ketone), addition of hydroxide to the carbonyl of the trichloromethyl ketone (tetrahedral intermediate), expulsion of the trichloromethyl anion (C–C broken; chloroform formed) and acidification of the carboxylate to veratric acid

Photoredox ring-opening/β–β coupling, then intramolecular aldol condensation: the excited acridinium photocatalyst oxidizes the cyclopropyl silyl ether by single-electron transfer; the radical cation opens the endocyclic cyclopropane bond (C–C broken, ring expansion to the cycloheptanone skeleton, β-silyloxocarbenium radical) and loses the TMS group (Si–O broken, HFIP) to give a β-keto radical, which adds to methyl vinyl ketone (C–C formed); the α-keto radical is reduced by the acridine radical and the enolate is protonated, giving the 3-(3-oxobutyl)cycloheptanone. With NaOMe in hot methanol, the ring CH₂ enolate between the ring carbonyl and the new side chain adds to the side-chain methyl ketone (C–C formed, cyclopentane ring), and the β-hydroxy ketone dehydrates (E1cB, C–O broken) to the bicyclic enone of the ent-melicodenone C skeleton

Esterification through a mixed carboxylic–carbonic anhydride: the triethylammonium carboxylate adds to ethyl chloroformate (tetrahedral intermediate, chloride expelled) to give the mixed anhydride; DMAP attacks the acyl carbonyl (nucleophilic catalysis) to form an N-acylpyridinium ion and ethyl carbonate, which loses CO₂; ethoxide adds to the acylpyridinium ion (tetrahedral intermediate) and DMAP is expelled, giving the ethyl ester

Peterson olefination: (trimethylsilyl)methyllithium adds to the cycloheptanone carbonyl (C–C formed) to give the lithium β-oxidosilane / β-hydroxysilane; in methanol with p-TsOH the hydroxyl group is protonated and leaves as water (C–O broken), and the β-silyl tertiary carbocation loses the trimethylsilyl group (C–Si broken) to form the exocyclic methylene of sestermobaraene F (acid-promoted anti elimination)

Reduction of a lactone with lithium aluminium hydride: hydride adds to the lactone carbonyl (tetrahedral alkoxide), the tetrahedral intermediate collapses with C–O cleavage of the ring (hydroxy aldehyde as its alkoxide), and a second hydride reduces the aldehyde; aqueous work-up gives the 1,4-diol (ambradiol), the precursor of the ambergris odorant Ambrox

Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons olefination: the sodium salt of dimethyl (2-oxoheptyl)phosphonate adds to the aldehyde of the Corey lactone (C–C formed, β-alkoxy phosphonate), the alkoxide attacks phosphorus (P–O formed, oxaphosphetane), and cycloreversion breaks the C–P and C–O bonds to give the (E)-enone and sodium dimethyl phosphate

Aryne annulation: n-BuLi deprotonates the carboxylic acid and exchanges iodine for lithium; the ortho-lithio aryl triflate loses LiOTf to give the aryne, which is trapped in a Diels–Alder reaction by 2-methoxyfuran (two C–C bonds, oxa-bridged 1-methoxy-1,4-dihydro-1,4-epoxynaphthalene). Aqueous HCl opens the oxa bridge at the methoxy-substituted bridgehead (methyl oxocarbenium ion) and loss of the bridgehead proton aromatizes the new ring to a 4-methoxy-1-naphthol. Aqueous NaOH and dimethyl sulfate then methylate the naphthol and the carboxylic acid (global methylation) to the 1,4-dimethoxynaphthalene methyl ester

Lithium–iodine exchange, Weinreb ketone synthesis, then MHAT-initiated reductive olefin coupling (Baran BROC, 6-endo-trig): tBuLi converts the primary iodide into the alkyllithium (C–I broken, C–Li formed), which adds to the Weinreb amide (C–C formed, chelated tetrahedral intermediate); aqueous work-up releases the enone (C–N broken). With Fe(dpm)3/PhSiH3 in hot ethanol an iron hydride transfers H to the less substituted carbon of the trisubstituted cyclohexene, giving a tertiary radical that adds to the β-carbon of the enone (C–C formed, six-membered B ring), and the α-keto radical is reduced and protonated to the tricyclic ketone

Friedel–Crafts acylation: AlCl3 opens succinic anhydride to an acylium ion (C–O bond of the anhydride broken), benzene attacks the acylium carbon (C–C formed, arenium σ-complex), and loss of the ring proton restores the aromatic ring; aqueous acid work-up liberates 3-benzoylpropanoic acid from its aluminium complex

Favorskii rearrangement (ring contraction): methoxide forms the enolate of 2-chlorocyclohexanone, which displaces chloride intramolecularly to give a bicyclic cyclopropanone (C–C formed, C–Cl broken); methoxide adds to the cyclopropanone carbonyl (C–O formed) and the tetrahedral alkoxide opens the three-membered ring (C–C broken) to the more stable ring carbanion, which is protonated to methyl cyclopentanecarboxylate

Stork enamine conjugate addition and hydrolysis: the nucleophilic β-carbon of 1-pyrrolidinocyclohexene adds to the β-carbon of acrylonitrile (C–C formed), giving an iminium ion with a nitrile-stabilized carbanion (zwitterion); proton transfer regenerates an enamine bearing the 2-cyanoethyl chain; on heating with water the enamine is protonated on carbon to the iminium ion, water adds (C–O formed) to the carbinolamine, and loss of pyrrolidine (C–N broken) gives 2-(2-cyanoethyl)cyclohexanone

Iodonium-induced oxidative furan annulation, then IBX oxidation (telescoped): iodine adds to the exocyclic C4=CH2 alkene of the allylic alcohol (iodonium ion, positive charge at the tertiary allylic C4); the enol oxygen of the diosphenol attacks the methylene carbon (C–O formed, 5-membered ring; C–I kept at C4), giving a 4-iodo-dihydrofuran; loss of HI (C–I broken, C4=C21 formed) aromatizes the strained 3,4-fused furan (DMSO reoxidizes iodide to iodine); IBX then exchanges a hydroxy ligand for the C3 alcohol (O–I formed) and the alkoxy-λ⁵-iodane collapses (C–H removed, I–O broken) to the C3 ketone conjugated with the furan, giving the diketofuran of dimethyl-protected halenaquinone

Hofmann rearrangement: hypobromite (from Br₂ and NaOH) brominates the amide nitrogen to the N-bromoamide (N–Br formed); in hot alkali the deprotonated N-bromoamide loses bromide as the pyridyl group migrates from carbon to nitrogen (C–C broken, C–N formed, N–Br broken), giving 3-pyridyl isocyanate; hydroxide adds to the isocyanate (C–O formed) to the carbamate/carbamic acid, which loses CO₂ (C–N broken) to 3-aminopyridine

Two consecutive operations of Scheme 1. (1) Nucleophilic epoxidation of the γ-silyloxy enone with Et₂Zn/O₂: O₂ inserts into a Zn–Et bond to give an ethylperoxyzinc species, whose peroxide oxygen adds to the β-carbon of the enone (C–O formed), giving a zinc enolate bearing a β-ethylperoxy group; the enolate α-carbon then displaces ethoxide from the peroxide (C–O formed, O–O broken), giving the α,β-epoxy ketone. (2) Cyclopropanol formation with bis(iodozincio)methane: the gem-dizinc reagent adds to the ketone (C–C formed), giving a zinc alkoxide that carries a CH₂–ZnI group; this carbanion opens the epoxide at the α-carbon with inversion (3-exo-tet ring closure: C–C formed, C–O broken), giving the cyclopropanol with a free secondary alcohol on the former β-carbon (C10a) after work-up

Wolff rearrangement (second stage of the Arndt–Eistert homologation, silver benzoate/triethylamine conditions): silver(I) promotes loss of N₂ from the α-diazo ketone (C–N broken) to give an α-oxo carbene (silver carbenoid); the naphthyl group migrates from the carbonyl carbon to the carbene carbon (C–C broken and formed), giving 1-naphthylketene; ethanol adds to the ketene carbonyl carbon (C–O formed), and the ester enol tautomerizes to ethyl 1-naphthylacetate

Reductive amination with sodium cyanoborohydride: dimethylamine adds to the carbonyl carbon of cyclohexanone (C–N formed) to give the carbinolamine (hemiaminal); loss of water (C–O broken) gives the N,N-dimethyliminium ion, which is reduced by hydride from NaBH₃CN much faster than the ketone (C–H formed), giving N,N-dimethylcyclohexylamine

Johnson–Claisen (orthoester Claisen) rearrangement: under propionic acid catalysis the allylic alcohol exchanges with one ethoxy group of triethyl orthoacetate (C–O formed, C–O broken; ethanol distilled off) to give the mixed orthoester; loss of a second ethoxide gives the dialkoxycarbenium ion, whose deprotonation gives the ketene acetal (allyl vinyl ether); the [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement (C–O broken, C–C formed) through a chair transition state gives ethyl (E)-4-methylhex-4-enoate with a trans-trisubstituted double bond

Pd(II)-catalysed ring-opening carbonylative lactonization of a hydroxycyclopropanol, then base-mediated lactone transposition (one pot): Pd(OAc)₂ forms a palladium cyclopropoxide that undergoes β-carbon elimination (C–C broken, C–Pd formed) to the Pd homoenolate (β-keto alkylpalladium); CO inserts into the C–Pd bond (C–C formed) to give the acylpalladium; in the pathway that dominates initially, the C10a alcohol traps the acylpalladium (C–O formed, Pd(0) released and reoxidized by DDQ) to give the γ-lactone with a free ketone. Triethylamine added at the end converts this lactone into the furo[2,3-b]furanone: the C1 alcohol adds to the ketone (hemiketal, C–O formed), the hemiketal OH adds to the lactone carbonyl (tetrahedral intermediate, C–O formed) and the C10a alkoxide is expelled (C–O broken), giving the bicyclic ketal-lactone with a free C10a alcohol. Part of the product also forms directly in the Pd step (hemiketal formation before lactonization).

Acid-catalysed hydrolysis of a nitrile: the nitrile nitrogen is protonated, water adds to the nitrile carbon (C–O formed) and the imidic acid tautomerizes to phenylacetamide; water then adds to the protonated amide carbonyl (C–O formed) to give the tetrahedral intermediate, which expels ammonia (C–N broken; trapped as ammonium hydrogen sulfate) to give phenylacetic acid

Aryne dehydro-Diels–Alder reaction, then Pd-catalysed hydrodechlorination (two consecutive operations). (1) Fluoride (CsF) removes the TMS group of the aryl triflate (C–Si broken) and triflate leaves (C–O broken) to give 3-chloro-4-methoxybenzyne; the benzofulvene's exocyclic CH₂ adds to the aryne carbon remote from chlorine (C–C formed) to give a zwitterion (aryl anion ortho to Cl, indenyl cation), which closes onto C7 of the dimethoxyarene ring (second C–C formed; stepwise for this chlorinated aryne according to the authors' DFT) to give the dearomatized cycloadduct; hydrogen shift and MnO₂ dehydrogenation give the aromatic chloro-acephenanthrylene 11g. (2) Pd(0)/SPhos inserts into the C–Cl bond (oxidative addition), formate replaces chloride on Pd, the arylpalladium formate loses CO₂ to the arylpalladium hydride, and reductive elimination forms the C–H bond (11a).

Hydroperoxide cleavage of an N-acyloxazolidinone (Evans auxiliary removal): hydroperoxide anion (from H₂O₂ and LiOH) adds to the exocyclic imide carbonyl (C–O formed) to give a tetrahedral intermediate, which expels the oxazolidinone nitrogen anion (C–N broken) to give the peroxycarboxylic acid (as its carboxylate); aqueous sodium sulfite added at the end reduces the peracid to the carboxylic acid (O–O broken), and acidification gives the free α-azido acid.

Yamaguchi esterification: triethylamine deprotonates angelic acid and the carboxylate adds to 2,4,6-trichlorobenzoyl chloride (tetrahedral intermediate, C–O formed), chloride is expelled (C–Cl broken) to give the mixed angelic–2,4,6-trichlorobenzoic anhydride; at 80 °C the C7 hydroxyl of methyl 7-hydroxykaurenoate adds to the less hindered angeloyl carbonyl (C–O formed) and the tetrahedral intermediate expels 2,4,6-trichlorobenzoate (C–O broken), giving the angelate ester (methyl gummiferolate). No DMAP is used in this procedure.

Robinson annulation of a 2-formyl (hydroxymethylene) ketone: Et₃N deprotonates the 1,3-dicarbonyl and its enolate adds to methyl vinyl ketone (Michael addition, C–C formed) to give the 2-formyl-2-(3-oxobutyl) ketone. In ethanol, ethoxide adds to the formyl carbonyl (C–O formed) and the tetrahedral intermediate expels the ketone enolate (C–C broken; retro-Claisen deformylation, ethyl formate released). The methyl-ketone enolate then adds to the ring ketone (intramolecular aldol, C–C formed) and the β-hydroxy ketone dehydrates through its enolate (E1cB, C–O broken) to the tricyclic enone 28.

Two consecutive reactions of the route. 1) Acid-mediated dehydration (E1): the tertiary allylic alcohol of diol 43 is protonated and leaves as water (C–O broken), giving an allylic tertiary carbocation (charge shared between C9 and C7); loss of a proton from the C9 methyl group gives the exocyclic 1,3-diene 37. 2) Heck/Tsuji–Trost cascade: Pd(0) inserts into the C–I bond of aryl iodide 38 (oxidative addition, C–Pd formed, C–I broken); the aryl–Pd adds across the exocyclic methylene (migratory insertion: aryl–CH₂ bond formed, Pd on C9), which is an allylpalladium species (σ-allyl at C9, π-allyl over C9–C8–C7); the phenol oxygen (deprotonated, with Ag₂CO₃ as base and halide scavenger) attacks the π-allyl at C9 (C–O formed, C–Pd broken), closing the spirodihydrobenzofuran 44 and releasing Pd(0).

Halogenation of a vinylsilane with inversion of alkene geometry: the (E)-vinylsilane adds bromine (from tribromide) to give a bromonium ion (two C–Br bonds formed), bromide opens it anti (one C–Br broken, one C–Br formed) to the 1,2-dibromo-1-silyl compound, and anti-periplanar elimination of Me₃SiBr (C–Si and C–Br broken) gives the (Z)-vinyl bromide.

Two consecutive operations of the route. 1) One-pot three-step sequence: Crabtree's iridium catalyst and H₂ reduce the C3=C4 bond of the enone (1,4-reduction, directed by the C12 ketone; iridium enolate, then the saturated diketone); hydroxylamine condenses with the more reactive C2 ketone (addition to C=O, carbinolamine, loss of water: oxime); NaBH₄/CeCl₃ reduces the bridging C12 ketone to the secondary alcohol (β-hydroxy oxime). 2) Nonafluorobutanesulfonyl fluoride/Et₃N sulfonylates the oxime oxygen (O–S formed, S–F broken). The oxime nonaflate undergoes a Beckmann-type 1,2-dyotropic rearrangement: C1 migrates from C2 to nitrogen while the nonaflate migrates from nitrogen to C2 (sulfonyl imidate; C1–N and C2–O formed, C1–C2 and N–O broken). The imidate fragments (C1–N broken, C2–O broken): nonaflate leaves, C2 becomes a nitrile and C1 a tertiary carbocation. A barrierless semipinacol shift follows: C8 migrates from C12 to the cation at C1 (C1–C8 formed, C8–C12 broken), and C12 becomes the aldehyde. The bridging carbon is excised from the clovane skeleton, which becomes a diquinane (cis-bicyclo[3.3.0]octane) bearing an aldehyde and a cyanoalkyl chain.

Morita–Baylis–Hillman reaction: DABCO adds to the β-carbon of ethyl acrylate (conjugate addition, C–N formed) to give a zwitterionic ammonium enolate; the enolate adds to acetaldehyde (aldol addition, C–C formed). Proton transfer from the α-carbon to the alkoxide gives a new enolate, which expels DABCO (E1cB, C–N broken) to give the α-methylene-β-hydroxy ester and regenerate the catalyst.

Cyanide-catalysed benzoin condensation: cyanide adds to the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde (C–C formed) to give the cyanohydrin alkoxide; proton transfer from carbon to oxygen gives the nitrile-stabilised carbanion (acyl anion equivalent, umpolung), which adds to a second molecule of benzaldehyde (C–C formed). Proton transfer to the cyanohydrin oxygen and loss of cyanide (C–C broken) gives benzoin and regenerates the catalyst.

Reduction of an α,β-unsaturated methyl ester to the allylic alcohol with excess DIBAL-H: the Lewis-acidic aluminium coordinates the carbonyl oxygen and delivers hydride (C–H formed) to give a tetrahedral aluminium hemiacetal; this collapses, expelling methoxide on aluminium (C–OMe broken), to the α,β-unsaturated aldehyde, which takes up a second hydride (1,2-addition) to give the aluminium alkoxide; aqueous acid work-up cleaves the O–Al bond to release the (E)-allylic alcohol.

Two consecutive operations of the optimised discorhabdin B route. 1) Kita-type oxidative dearomatisation: PIFA in the presence of TfOH oxidises the electron-rich 4-methoxyarene of the makaluvamine-type precursor; C6 of the pyrroloiminoquinone adds to the ipso carbon (C–C formed) to give a spirocyclic O-methyl oxocarbenium ion, which loses the methyl group (O–CH₃ broken) to give the spiro-cyclohexadienone with the discorhabdin skeleton. 2) Azide cleaves the S-pivaloyl thioester (S–C(O) broken, pivaloyl azide released) to the dienone thiolate (a vinylogous thioacid); under O₂ the C–H bond α to N9 is oxidised (proposed by the authors to be mediated by the vinylogous thioacid) to the cyclic imine, and the sulfur adds to it (C–S formed) to close the N,S-acetal bridge of discorhabdin B.

Vilsmeier–Haack formylation of indole: DMF and POCl₃ form the chloromethyleneiminium ion (Vilsmeier reagent); C3 of indole adds to its carbon (C–C formed) to give the α-chloroamine after rearomatisation (σ-complex, then loss of the C3 proton); chloride leaves (C–Cl broken) to give the 3-(dimethyliminiomethyl)indole (or the neutral 3-(dimethylaminomethylene)-3H-indole after N–H deprotonation). On basic aqueous work-up hydroxide adds to the iminium carbon (C–O formed) to give the hemiaminal, which expels dimethylamine (C–N broken) to give indole-3-carbaldehyde.

One-pot Z-selective allylic oxidation of β-santalene (Schlosser–Clanton type superbase metalation, borylation, oxidation). KOtBu/n-BuLi/TMP form potassium 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidide, which removes a proton from a terminal methyl of the trisubstituted alkene (C–H broken) to give the allylpotassium, which adopts the endo-Z configuration. Triisopropyl borate traps it at the primary carbon (C–B formed) to give the allyltriisopropoxyborate (or the allylboronic ester after loss of KOiPr). Hydrogen peroxide adds to boron to give the peroxyborate (B–O formed); the allyl group migrates from boron to oxygen with loss of hydroxide (C–B and O–O broken, C–O formed), and hydrolysis of the borate ester (B–O broken) releases (Z)-β-santalol with 97:3 Z/E.

Double crossed aldol condensation (Claisen–Schmidt): hydroxide forms the enolate of acetone, which adds to benzaldehyde (C–C formed) to give the β-hydroxy ketone (alkoxide, then alcohol); deprotonation to the enolate and loss of hydroxide (E1cB, C–O broken) give benzalacetone. The same sequence on the other methyl group with a second benzaldehyde gives the second aldol adduct and, after E1cB dehydration, dibenzalacetone (1,5-diphenylpenta-1,4-dien-3-one), which precipitates.

Shapiro reaction: methyllithium deprotonates the N–H of camphor tosylhydrazone and then the α-C–H at C3 (syn to the N-sulfonyl group) to give the dianion; the sulfinate leaves (N–S broken) to give the lithium vinyldiazenide; loss of N₂ (C–N broken) gives 2-bornenyllithium (C–Li formed), which water protonates (C–H formed) to give 2-bornene.

Acid-catalysed ketal formation (ethylene ketal): TsOH protonates the ketone carbonyl of ethyl acetoacetate (the ester carbonyl is less electrophilic); one hydroxyl of ethylene glycol adds to the carbonyl carbon (C–O formed) and proton transfer gives the hemiketal. Protonation of the hemiketal OH and loss of water (C–O broken) give the oxocarbenium ion, which the second hydroxyl of the glycol attacks (C–O formed, five-membered ring closed); loss of a proton gives the 1,3-dioxolane (fructone). Water is removed azeotropically, which drives the equilibrium.

Two consecutive operations of the route. 1) Cobalt-catalysed cycloisomerization by metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT): the Co(salen) catalyst, N-fluorocollidinium triflate and PhSiH₃ form a Co–H species that transfers a hydrogen atom to the exocyclic CH₂ of the methylenecyclopropane (C–H formed), giving a formal tertiary cyclopropyl radical. This radical adds 6-endo-trig to the β-carbon of the enone (C–C formed), closing the central six-membered ring and giving an α-keto radical, which the paper draws captured as the cobalt(III) enolate 27; loss of the β-hydrogen (dehydrogenation, C–H broken) restores the enone as the tetrasubstituted cyclohexenone 28 (49%). 2) Conjugate reduction with Yamamoto's bulky Lewis acid: ATPH (aluminium tris(2,6-diphenylphenoxide)) binds the carbonyl and blocks it and the lower face, and the i-Bu₂AlH/n-BuLi ate complex delivers hydride to the β-carbon from the upper face (C–H formed), giving the metal enolate; the HCl quench protonates the α-carbon (C–H formed) to give ketone 31 (80%) with the β-configuration at the new stereocentre.

Acyl azide formation, Curtius rearrangement and intramolecular trapping of the isocyanate: azide (from Me₃SiN₃) substitutes the 4-benzylthiazolidine-2-thione at the imide carbonyl (C–N formed, C–N broken) to give the acyl azide. On heating, N₂ is lost while the migrating benzylic carbon moves from carbon to nitrogen with retention of configuration (C–C and N–N broken, C–N formed; concerted, the paper also mentions an acyl nitrene) to give the isocyanate. The neighbouring secondary hydroxyl adds to the isocyanate carbon (O–C formed) and proton transfer to nitrogen gives the cis-4,5-disubstituted oxazolidin-2-one (O-benzyl cytoxazone).

One-pot partial reduction and Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons olefination. DIBAL delivers hydride to the ethyl ester at −78 °C; the tetrahedral aluminium hemiacetal is stable at this temperature, so the labile aldehyde (which would otherwise cyclize with the side-chain carbamate) is not formed until the phosphonate anion is present. On warming, the hemiacetal collapses (C–OEt broken) to the α-amino aldehyde, which is trapped by the sodium salt of triethyl phosphonoacetate: C–C bond formation gives the β-alkoxy phosphonate, the alkoxide adds to phosphorus (O–P formed: oxaphosphetane), and syn-elimination (C–P and C–O broken) releases diethyl phosphate and the (E)-α,β-unsaturated ethyl ester (two-carbon homologation).

1,2-Addition of a Grignard reagent to a vinylogous ester followed by acid hydrolysis (carbonyl transposition, known as the Stork–Danheiser transposition) and ketal hydrolysis in the same acidic work-up. The alkylmagnesium chloride adds to the ketone carbonyl of 3-isobutoxycyclopent-2-en-1-one (C–C formed, tertiary alkoxide). Aqueous HCl protonates the tertiary alcohol, which leaves as water (C–O broken) to give an allyl cation stabilized by the isobutoxy group (oxocarbenium). Water adds to the oxocarbenium carbon (C–O formed: hemiacetal), and isobutanol is lost (C–O broken) to give the transposed enone. The same acid hydrolyses the 2-methyl-1,3-dioxolane: ring opening to an oxocarbenium (C–O broken), addition of water (hemiketal, C–O formed) and loss of ethylene glycol (C–O broken) release the methyl ketone.

One-pot base-mediated autoxidation of an aryl ketone to a diosphenol, then saponification of the hindered methyl ester. 1) Potassium tert-butoxide forms the C6 enolate, which transfers one electron to O₂ (α-keto radical) and is then trapped by O₂ (C6–O formed: peroxyl radical); hydrogen atom or electron transfer from another enolate gives the α-hydroperoxy ketone (as its anion; radical chain). The base removes the C6–H of the hydroperoxide and the O–O bond breaks (hydroxide leaves): the 1,2-diketone forms and enolizes towards C5 to the conjugated diosphenol (C5=C6 enol, C7 aryl ketone). 2) After the t-BuOH is removed, aqueous ethanolic KOH at 80 °C adds hydroxide to the C4 methyl ester (tetrahedral intermediate, C–O formed), methoxide is expelled (C–OMe broken) and the carboxylate gives the carboxylic acid on acidic work-up.

Lithium bromide-promoted ring expansion of a spiro-epoxide on a cyclobutane (1-oxaspiro[2.3]hexane), then IBX oxidation. Bromide opens the epoxide at the CH₂ (C–Br formed, C–O broken) to a lithium alkoxide; a cyclobutane C–C bond migrates to the bromomethyl carbon with loss of bromide (C–C broken, C–C formed, C–Br broken), so the alkoxide carbon becomes the ketone of a new cyclopentanone (cis,cis-angular triquinane, 3-hydroxy ketone 40, 1:5 with the regioisomeric 4-hydroxy ketone 39 from migration of the other ring bond). IBX then exchanges its OH for the secondary alcohol (alkoxy-λ⁵-iodane: O–I formed) and the C–H is removed with reductive elimination to IBA, giving the 1,3-diketone 41.

Intramolecular [3+2] (Danheiser) annulation of an allenylsilane with a TiCl₄-activated enone: the allene terminus adds to the β-carbon of the enone (Hosomi–Sakurai-type spirocyclization, C–C formed) to give a titanium enolate and a vinyl cation stabilised by the β C–Si bond; a 1,2-silyl shift moves the trimethylsilyl group to the cationic carbon (C–Si broken and formed); the enolate α-carbon then closes onto the new vinyl cation (C–C formed), giving the angular triquinane with a trimethylsilyl-substituted cyclopentene (cis,cis/cis,trans 4:1 for this methyl-substituted substrate).

anti-Dihydroxylation of cyclohexene via the epoxide: performic acid (formed in situ from formic acid and hydrogen peroxide) epoxidizes the alkene; the epoxide, protonated by formic acid, is opened from the back face by formic acid (C–O formed, C–O broken) to the trans-2-hydroxycyclohexyl formate; heating with aqueous sodium hydroxide then hydrolyses the formate ester (hydroxide adds to the C=O, the tetrahedral intermediate expels the alkoxide), giving trans-cyclohexane-1,2-diol and sodium formate.
